subject: Information Theory
title: Medical Imaging
description: A quick, practical guide to Medical Imaging.

hook.text: An MRI scanner sees inside your body without a single cut. Pure signal processing turns radio echoes into anatomy.

buildup.text: MRI excites hydrogen atoms with radio pulses. Different tissues relax at different rates, creating contrast.

discovery.text: Fourier transforms convert the raw signals from frequency space into spatial images—slice by precise slice.

twist.text: Noise limits resolution. Signal averaging, surface coils, and compressed sensing push quality further each decade.

climax.text: From X-rays to CT to MRI to ultrasound, every medical image is a triumph of signal extraction from noise.

punchline.text: Radio waves in, anatomy out. Signal processing saves lives.

quiz.question: What role does signal processing play in MRI?
options: It converts radio signals into anatomical images
